learning_outcomes.text: Knows the properties of transformers, induction motors and synchronous generators as basic elements of the power system, in steady and transient states.
Knows the properties of transformers, induction motors and synchronous generators under asymmetric supply conditions.
Knows and understands the impact of transient states of electric motors and generators on the quality of electrical energy in the network in which they operate.
Knows and understands the economic aspects of voltage regulation with frequency control of induction motors.
Understands the economic and practical aspects of parallel operation of transformers and its conditions.
Knows the principles and methods of identification of parameters of mathematical models of electrical machines.
Can use catalog parameters of transformers, induction motors and synchronous generators to assess their properties in steady and transient states and under asymmetric supply conditions.
Can assess currents and torques in asynchronous operating states of a generator and their impact on electrical energy quality.
Can propose, perform and process measurement results to determine the parameters and properties of a transformer, induction motor and synchronous generator as basic elements of the power system.
The student can work in a group and cooperate with it in carrying out a research topic, both in the measurement and computer laboratory.
The student can prepare a report and documentation of the conducted research in the measurement laboratory and properly process the measurement results and draw conclusions.

syllabus_topics: Laboratory exercises: Modern measurement systems for machines and characteristics of real machines. 8 two-hour exercises:
Three-phase transformer. General tests. Measurement of parameters.
Inverter supply of an induction motor.
Three-phase cage induction machine.
Induction motor.
Synchronous generator. Parameter measurements. Standalone operation.
Synchronous machine. Cooperation with the grid.
DC motor.
Universal motor.
Problems analyzed in auditorium classes:
1- and 3-phase transformer: parameter model identification, calculating voltage drop on a loaded transformer, calculating transformer efficiency for a given operating point (2 hours).

Operation of a three-phase transformer under asymmetric supply: analysis of equivalent circuits for positive, negative, and zero sequence components for various winding connection schemes, calculating winding currents under asymmetric supply (2 hours).

Frequency control of induction machine speed: analysis of mechanical characteristics of an induction machine with frequency change, influence of stator resistance on the shape of characteristics, calculating speed, current, and torque of an induction machine at a given operating point with frequency supply change (2 hours).

Operation of an induction machine under asymmetric supply: analysis of mechanical characteristics under asymmetric supply, calculating stator phase currents of a loaded induction machine under asymmetric supply (2 hours).

Statics of salient-pole synchronous machine: phasor diagram of salient-pole synchronous machine, V-curves, power factor regulation, calculating power angle, electromagnetic torque, stator current, power factor for a given operating point (2 hours).

Standalone operation of a salient-pole synchronous machine: calculating external characteristics, calculating current and voltage of a receiver supplied by a salient-pole synchronous machine (1 hour).

Statics of synchronous machine with permanent magnets: phasor diagram of PMAC synchronous machine, calculating power angle, electromagnetic torque, stator current, power factor for a given operating point (2 hours).
Two control works (2 hours).
Lectures: THREE-PHASE POWER TRANSFORMERS
Three-phase power transformers, construction, equivalent circuit and parameter identification, no-load operation, voltage variability, efficiency (2 hours).
Parallel operation of transformers, conditions for parallel operation, selection of transformers for parallel operation, equivalent circuit of transformers operating in parallel (2 hours).
Operation of a three-phase transformer under external asymmetry, equivalent circuits for various connection arrangements, methods for calculating currents. (2 hours).
ROTATING ELECTRICAL MACHINES, DYNAMICS, CONTROL, OPERATION UNDER VARIOUS SUPPLY CONDITIONS
Three-phase induction machine under asymmetric voltage supply. Single-phase induction machine (2 hours).
Dynamic equations of an induction machine, 0dq mathematical model for dynamic states, transformation matrix, purpose of coordinate transformation (2 hours).
Frequency control of an induction machine. Principles of scalar and vector control. Application of 0dq transformation to vector control. (2 hours).

Salient-pole synchronous machine, construction and properties in steady and dynamic states. Two-axis model of a 3-phase salient-pole synchronous machine – equations for dynamic states in 0dq coordinates, transformation matrix, purpose of coordinate transformation (2 hours).

Three-phase salient-pole synchronous generator operating in an isolated grid in steady state, basic characteristics: no-load, short-circuit, external, regulation. Additional conditions for energy conversion in a synchronous machine (2 hours).

Salient-pole synchronous machine cooperating with the power grid in steady state – rotating field, phasor diagram, power angle, motor and generator operation, power factor regulation, V-curves (2 hours).
ELECTRICAL MACHINES IN RENEWABLE ENERGY AND ELECTROMOBILITY
PM BLDC motors. Construction, operating principle, electronic commutator. Examples of applications in vehicle drives (2 hours).
PMAC machines. Construction, operating principle and control. Examples of application in generation and drive systems (2 hours).
Reluctance motors. Construction, operating principle and control, and applications in drive systems (2 hours).
Doubly-fed machine. Construction, operating principle and control. Application of DFIG in wind power plants. (4 hours).
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed by a final exam. Auditorium classes are assessed by obtaining a positive grade from mid-semester colloquia. Laboratory classes require passing all laboratory exercises, which is based on presenting a solution to the given problem. Students are obliged to prepare for laboratory exercises, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium.
